pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Water can disappear from view by seeping into a porous surface, by evaporating into water vapour, or by both processes depending on the surface.
pedagogy.lok_folk: When water is no longer visible, it must have gone down into the surface underneath it.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Says evaporation or seepage with no surface check.
Says both for puddles but keeps seepage for steel.

units.subject: science
units.chapter_title: A journey through states of water
units.decision_hinge: Decide what liquid water becomes when it evaporates or when water sprinkled on a hot pan disappears.
units.mechanism: Evaporation is the conversion of liquid water into its vapour state; steam is water vapour, with visible droplets making part of it visible.

mx.cwo: Evaporation is when water vapour turns back into liquid water, so the hot-pan water became droplets first.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Evaporation is the conversion of liquid water into its vapour state; steam is water vapour, with visible droplets making part of it visible.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Steam is smoke or visible mist, not water in another state.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Uses steam, vapour, and droplets while giving the wrong state-change direction.
Matches the hot-pan observation but avoids naming the state produced.

units.subject: science
units.chapter_title: A journey through states of water
units.decision_hinge: Decide where the droplets on the outside of a cold glass come from.
units.mechanism: When water vapour in the air touches a cold surface, it changes into liquid water droplets by condensation.

mx.cwo: The droplets on the outside of the cold tumbler are water that seeped out from inside the glass.
The outside drops are melted ice that came through the glass wall.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: When water vapour in the air touches a cold surface, it changes into liquid water droplets by condensation.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Water seen on a glass must have leaked from the water or ice inside it.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Says condensation without naming air vapour or cold glass contact.
Mentions cold glass but assigns drops to inside water or melted ice.

units.subject: science
units.chapter_title: A journey through states of water
units.decision_hinge: Decide whether a sample is behaving as a solid, liquid, or gas based on shape, flow, and spreading.
units.mechanism: A solid keeps its shape, a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping its volume, and a gas spreads through the available space without a fixed shape.

mx.cwo: Liquid water poured into a bowl is a solid because it has the bowl's shape.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: A solid keeps its shape, a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping its volume, and a gas spreads through the available space without a fixed shape.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Shape alone tells the state; if something has any shape at the moment, it is solid.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Names ice, water, and vapour states from memory without property evidence.
Mentions shape but ignores flow and spreading.

units.subject: science
units.chapter_title: A journey through states of water
units.decision_hinge: Decide which state change occurs when water or another substance is heated or cooled.
units.mechanism: Heating can change solid to liquid by melting and liquid to gas by evaporation; cooling can change gas to liquid by condensation and liquid to solid by freezing.

mx.cwo: Heating liquid water freezes it into ice, and cooling ice evaporates it into water vapour.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Heating can change solid to liquid by melting and liquid to gas by evaporation; cooling can change gas to liquid by condensation and liquid to solid by freezing.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Heating and cooling are just ways to change state, so the process names can be used in any direction.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Names melting, freezing, evaporation, or condensation without showing direction.

units.subject: science
units.chapter_title: A journey through states of water
units.decision_hinge: Decide which conditions make water evaporate faster or slower.
units.mechanism: Water evaporates faster when more surface is exposed to air, when it is warmer or in sunlight, and when air has less water vapour; it evaporates slower in humid air.

mx.cwo: The water in the bottle cap evaporates faster than the same amount spread on a plate because the cap has less exposed area.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Water evaporates faster when more surface is exposed to air, when it is warmer or in sunlight, and when air has less water vapour; it evaporates slower in humid air.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Only the amount of water controls evaporation time; exposed area, sunlight, wind, and humidity do not matter.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Gives the faster case without explaining the condition.
Says sunny or windy dries faster without linking to evaporation.

units.subject: science
units.chapter_title: A journey through states of water
units.decision_hinge: Decide why evaporation can make water, skin, or surroundings feel cooler.
units.mechanism: Evaporation produces a cooling effect on the remaining water or nearby surface.

mx.cwo: Evaporation makes the remaining water warmer, so water in an earthen pot becomes hot as water evaporates through it.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Evaporation produces a cooling effect on the remaining water or nearby surface.
pedagogy.lok_folk: An earthen pot or fan cools only because the clay or moving air is already cold, not because water evaporates.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Mentions evaporation or cooling without saying what evaporates and what becomes cooler.
Says evaporation changes temperature but avoids whether it cools or warms.

units.subject: science
units.chapter_title: A journey through states of water
units.decision_hinge: Decide how water vapour becomes clouds and rain, hail, or snow.
units.mechanism: Water vapour rises, cools, condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds, and many droplets together fall as rain, hail, or snow.

mx.cwo: Water vapour falls as rain first and then condenses into cloud droplets near the ground.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Water vapour rises, cools, condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds, and many droplets together fall as rain, hail, or snow.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Clouds are just invisible water vapour collected overhead, so droplets are not needed before rain.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Uses vapour, cloud, and rain terms while hiding the rain-first reversal.

units.subject: science
units.chapter_title: A journey through states of water
units.decision_hinge: Decide how water moves between Earth's surface, the atmosphere, and back again in the water cycle.
units.mechanism: In the water cycle, water from oceans and Earth's surface evaporates into the atmosphere as vapour, returns as rain, hail, or snow, and ultimately flows back to the oceans.

mx.cwo: Condensation moves ocean water up into the atmosphere, and evaporation brings rain, hail, or snow back down.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: In the water cycle, water from oceans and Earth's surface evaporates into the atmosphere as vapour, returns as rain, hail, or snow, and ultimately flows back to the oceans.
pedagogy.lok_folk: The water cycle is just rain falling into rivers; the return to atmosphere and back to oceans is not connected.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Names ocean, cloud, rain, river, lake, groundwater, evaporation, and condensation.
Uses evaporation and condensation in a full-sounding cycle explanation.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide whether separation is being done to remove an unwanted component or to collect useful components.
units.mechanism: Substances are separated either to remove a component that is not useful or to separate different useful components from a mixture.

mx.cwo: Separating stones from grains is done to collect useful stones; the grains are the part to throw away.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Substances are separated either to remove a component that is not useful or to separate different useful components from a mixture.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Separation always means the removed part is the useful part.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Says stones and grains were separated without saying which part is kept.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when handpicking is the suitable separation method for a solid mixture.
units.mechanism: Handpicking separates solid materials from a mixture when the components can be picked out by hand because they differ in size, colour, or shape.

mx.cwo: Use handpicking to remove husk from 50 kg of wheat.
Use threshing to remove whole black peppers from a plate of pulao.
Use handpicking for 10 kg of rice mixed with tiny white husk because the pieces are not easy to see.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Handpicking separates solid materials from a mixture when the components can be picked out by hand because they differ in size, colour, or shape.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Any solid mixture should be separated by hand if a person has enough time.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Says handpicking for grains without explaining why it fits.
Uses a chapter process name without matching the action.
Mentions visibility but makes hard-to-see pieces support handpicking.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when threshing is needed before separating grains from husk.
units.mechanism: Threshing is the process in which stalks are beaten to separate grains from them.

mx.cwo: Threshing is done after the grains are already loose; it separates husk from loose grains.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Threshing is the process in which stalks are beaten to separate grains from them.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Threshing is just another word for cleaning grain after harvest.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: names threshing
mentions husk separation after harvest

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when winnowing can separate a mixture using moving air.
units.mechanism: Winnowing separates heavier and lighter components of a mixture by wind or by blowing air.

mx.cwo: Winnow rice and husk in a closed room with no wind; the husk will still blow away.
During winnowing, the heavier wheat grains blow far away and the lighter husk falls near the farmer.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Winnowing separates heavier and lighter components of a mixture by wind or by blowing air.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Winnowing works because the tray is shaken, so wind is not necessary.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Uses the word winnowing for the separation.
Mentions wind but not which component is carried farther.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when sieving is suitable for separating solid particles by size.
units.mechanism: Sieving allows smaller particles to pass through the holes of a sieve while bigger particles remain on the sieve.

mx.cwo: In sieving flour, the bigger bran and stones pass through the holes while the fine flour remains on the sieve.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Sieving allows smaller particles to pass through the holes of a sieve while bigger particles remain on the sieve.
pedagogy.lok_folk: A sieve keeps the wanted material on top, whatever its size is.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Uses sieve vocabulary while claiming bran and stones pass through.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when evaporation can recover a dissolved solid from a solution.
units.mechanism: Evaporation separates salt from a salt solution because water disappears or boils away and salt is left behind.

mx.cwo: Filter the salt solution through a cloth; 2 teaspoons of dissolved salt will stay on the cloth.
Heating the salt solution makes the salt evaporate away and the water stay in the dish.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Evaporation separates salt from a salt solution because water disappears or boils away and salt is left behind.
pedagogy.lok_folk: When water disappears from salt solution, the salt disappears along with it.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Says evaporation or water disappears without naming the salt residue.
Names a separation method without saying whether salt or water leaves.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when sedimentation followed by decantation can separate a liquid from heavier matter or a separate layer.
units.mechanism: Sedimentation is the settling down of a heavier insoluble component at the bottom of a liquid, and decantation is removing the liquid by tilting the vessel.

mx.cwo: After tea stands undisturbed, the tea leaves stay on top and the clear tea settles at the bottom.
Sedimentation and decantation remove every tea leaf from tea, so the poured cup has 0 tea leaves.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Sedimentation is the settling down of a heavier insoluble component at the bottom of a liquid, and decantation is removing the liquid by tilting the vessel.
pedagogy.lok_folk: If a liquid is poured gently, any solid impurity in it is completely removed.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Names sedimentation and decantation but says leaves stay on top.
Names both processes and says the poured cup has 0 leaves.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when filtration, rather than decantation alone, is needed to separate solid particles from a liquid.
units.mechanism: Filtration separates solid particles from a liquid by passing the mixture through a strainer, cloth, filter paper, or other filter with pores that hold back the particles and let the liquid pass.

mx.cwo: Use the same coarse tea strainer again; muddy water will become clear even though the mud particles pass through its holes.
In filtration with filter paper, mud particles pass through as filtrate and clear water stays on the paper as residue.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Filtration separates solid particles from a liquid by passing the mixture through a strainer, cloth, filter paper, or other filter with pores that hold back the particles and let the liquid pass.
pedagogy.lok_folk: All filters work the same way, so any strainer or cloth should make muddy water clear.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Says filtration is needed after muddy water remains.
Names filter paper for muddy water.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when churning is the suitable method for obtaining butter or cream from milk products.
units.mechanism: Churning is used to obtain butter from curd and is the method associated with separating cream from milk.

mx.cwo: Churning is the method for separating oil from water; it is not used for cream from milk.
When curd is churned, buttermilk floats at the top and butter stays at the bottom.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Churning is used to obtain butter from curd and is the method associated with separating cream from milk.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Churning means any mixing of a liquid, so it can separate any liquid mixture.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Learner writes churning only.
Learner selects churning but for oil-water.
Learner says curd is churned but reverses separated parts.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when magnetic separation can be used instead of handpicking.
units.mechanism: Magnetic separation separates magnetic and non-magnetic substances by using a magnet; iron is a common magnetic substance.

mx.cwo: A magnet pulls the sawdust away from iron nails because sawdust is magnetic and iron nails are non-magnetic.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Magnetic separation separates magnetic and non-magnetic substances by using a magnet; iron is a common magnetic substance.
pedagogy.lok_folk: A magnet is just a faster way to pick any visible solid from a mixture.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Says magnetic separation.
Mentions a magnet and sawdust or iron nails.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide when a mixture needs a sequence of several separation methods rather than one method.
units.mechanism: A mixture with more than two components requires a combination of several methods of separation.

mx.cwo: Use handpicking once on potatoes, salt, and sawdust; all 3 components will be separated.
Use evaporation first to separate the iron nails from sand, black pepper, stones, common salt, and water.
Choose evaporation before observing the components; the component properties do not decide the order.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: A mixture with more than two components requires a combination of several methods of separation.
pedagogy.lok_folk: One separation method should finish any mixture if it is done carefully enough.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Use handpicking once on potatoes, salt, and sawdust; all three components will be separated.
Use evaporation first to separate the iron nails from sand, black pepper, stones, common salt, and water.
Choose evaporation before observing the components; the component properties do not decide the order.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide whether something is living by checking the shared life characteristics rather than one visible sign.
units.mechanism: Living beings share a set of characteristics: they show movement, need food, grow, respire, excrete, respond to stimuli, reproduce, and die; non-living things do not show this set.

mx.cwo: The car is living because anything that moves on its own is living.
The plant is non-living because it does not move from one place to another like an animal.

pedagogy.mastery_signal: The learner correctly applies this rule: Living beings share a set of characteristics: they show movement, need food, grow, respire, excrete, respond to stimuli, reproduce, and die; non-living things do not show this set.
pedagogy.lok_folk: Something is living only if it visibly moves like an animal.

gaming_pockets.apparent_success: Names living or non-living without showing the life-process check.
Uses movement language that sounds chapter-based but skips the full set.

units.subject: science
units.decision_hinge: Decide whether a change in action is a response to a stimulus in a living being.
units.mechanism: A stimulus is a change or contact that can cause a living being to respond; animals and plants both show responses to stimuli.

mx.cwo: The touch-me-not leaves fold on their own; touching the plant is not needed for the response.
The hand pulling away from a hot cup should be counted only as movement, not as a response to a stimulus.
